common_name: Ancestral Anadromous Complete-Morph Stickleback (32 Lateral Plates)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Gasterosteus aculeatus_marine (52 µm, detail scale)

schnakenberg: du/dt = D_u laplacian(u) + a - u + u^2 v
dv/dt = D_v laplacian(v) + b - u^2 v
equations.dispersion_det: det(J - k^2 D) = D_u D_v k^4 - (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) k^2 + (f_u g_v - f_v g_u)
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)

boundary_conditions: Periodic on a square flank patch whose side is 12 marine critical wavelengths (624 µm). The patch is the integument between neighbouring lateral plates, not the whole 65 mm fish.
empirical_claims: Turing (1952): a homogeneous reaction-diffusion state can be unstable at a finite critical wavenumber k_c while remaining stable at k = 0.

Colosimo et al. (2005), DOI 10.1126/science.1107239: Ectodysplasin alleles repeatedly fix the complete versus low lateral-plate morph; low-plated haplotypes are old standing variation, and complete marine fish carry the ancestral plated phenotype.
Colosimo et al. (2004), DOI 10.1371/journal.pbio.0020109: low-morph siblings in their cross had eight or fewer anterior plates per side.

Bell, Baumgartner and Olson (1985), DOI 10.1017/S0094837300011581: six morphological characters of Miocene Gasterosteus doryssus change through the Truckee section, including armor-related traits; the section is not stasis.

Kondo and Asai (1995) and Nakamasu et al. (2009): teleost pigment bars are a reaction-diffusion pattern maintained by pigment-cell interactions. Those papers measure zebrafish and angelfish, not a 52 µm stickleback spacing.
what_changes_at_this_node: Relative to G. doryssus_late (9.99 Ma), the 0.015 Ma marine ancestor is the short-wavelength, high-k_c state: s drops from 4 to 1 and lambda drops from 104 µm to 52 µm as the complete 32-plate morph is re-established. Relative to living G. aculeatus, the marine ancestor remains shorter (52 µm versus 78 µm, s = 2.25). The organ-tier siblings at 1.7 mm and 2.4 mm are a different tier and are not reused as these cellular lengths.

specimen.creator: Holger Krisp
specimen.role: Extant G. aculeatus anatomical plate for computer-vision comparison. Not a Pleistocene fossil.

reported_in_source: Turing dispersion relation and critical wavenumber
Eda control of complete versus low plate morphs
Temporal change of armor characters in G. doryssus
reconstructed_in_script: Schnakenberg parameters placed so the marine critical wavelength is 52 µm
lambda(N) = 52 µm * sqrt(32/N) for the predecessor and successor scenarios
Specimen-locked gain that keeps the rendered flank spectrum correlated with the photograph
does_not_claim: That 52 µm was measured on a fossil melanophore
That N_eff = 8 is a plate count from the Truckee Formation
That the 2020 German photograph is the 15 ka marine ancestor
